Hemakūṭa
(‘mass of gold’)
------------------------------------------
This earth comprises seven dvīpas or islands. Each island has seven distinguishing mountains called ‘Kulaparvatas’.
Hemakūṭa is one of the seven Kulaparvatas of जम्बूद्वीप, the island where भारतवर्ष or India is situated. It is situated to the north of the हिमालयस्. On its two sides is situated the Lavaṇa-समुद्र or the ocean of salt. कुबेर’s capital city—Alakāpurī—rests on one of its peaks.
See also KULAPARVATAS.

Hemādri
------------------------------------------
Purāṇas and धर्मशास्त्रस् have played a very important part in moulding the Hindu society over the centuries.
Hemādri is one of the most prolific writers of the dharmaśāstra literature and his Caturvarga-cintāmaṇi has been considered as a classic.
His other works are: Āyurveda-rasāyana (a commentary on the Aṣṭāṅgahṛdaya of वाग्भट), a commentary on the Raghuvaṁśa of कालिदास, a commentary on शौनक’s Praṇavakalpa.
He belonged to the Vatsagotra. He was the grandson of वासुदेव and son of Kāmadeva. He was a high officer in the court of the Yādava kings महादेव and Rāmacandra of Devagiri (modern Daulatabad in Maharashtra). He must have existed in the 13th century A. D.
See CATURVARGA-CINTĀMAṆI also.

hemaśrāddha
(‘śrāddha with gold [or money]’)
------------------------------------------
Honouring the dead ancestors and gratefully remembering them on the day of their death has been an important religious duty of the Hindus. The ceremony conducted on such occasions is called ‘śrāddha’. (See ŚRĀDDHA for details.)
When a regular śrāddha cannot be performed due to some problems like अशौच or journey, it can be substituted with आमश्राद्ध (See ĀMAŚRĀDDHA for details.) or हेमश्राद्ध.
If in आमश्राद्ध, twice the quantity of grains (needed for cooked ड़ोओद् in a regular śrāddha) is given as gift, in हेमश्राद्ध, money needed for four times the quantity of grains has to be donated to worthy persons.
